# chezmoi-dotfiles

This machine's `$HOME` is managed by a **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system
deps) dotfiles repo. This skill is the agent-facing map: how to drive it, and what
custom tooling exists that you wouldn't otherwise know about. It is rendered per-host
— the "What's enabled on THIS machine" section reflects what the user actually
selected at init.

## Orientation (read this first)

- **Repo root**: `chezmoi source-path` (no args) prints the source dir. Work there
  to edit: `cd "$(chezmoi source-path)"`.
- **Source path of one file**: `chezmoi source-path ~/.config/foo/bar` → the
  managed source file for that target.
- **`docs/**` is NOT deployed to `$HOME`** (it's chezmoi-ignored). Read detail via
  `"$(chezmoi source-path)/docs/..."`. A *subset* is deployed to `~/.config/docs/`
  (e.g. keybindings, cli-tools) for runtime helpers.
- **Read the contract before editing**: `"$(chezmoi source-path)/CLAUDE.md"` holds
  Hard invariants and cross-file maintenance rules. Honor them.
- This host: profile `macos_intel`, OS `darwin`/`amd64`, primary shell `zsh`.

## chezmoi essentials

```bash
chezmoi diff                 # preview changes (also: just chezmoi-diff)
chezmoi apply                # deploy + run scripts (also: cas, or just chezmoi-apply)
chezmoi status               # modified/added/removed targets
chezmoi edit ~/.zshrc        # edit the SOURCE of a target
chezmoi add  ~/.config/x     # start managing an existing file
chezmoi re-add               # pull live edits back into source
chezmoi managed | grep foo   # is X managed?
chezmoi cat ~/.config/x      # render a target without applying
chezmoi data | jq            # the template data (ground truth for the toggles below)
```

- **`cas`** = `chezmoi apply` + reload hint; **`cau`** = update from remote then apply
  (defined in `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh`).
- **`dotcfg`** = reconfigure the init prompts on an already-set-up machine
  (`dotcfg` for the TUI, `dotcfg --set installLlmTools=true --yes` for one toggle,
  `dotcfg --dry-run` to preview). Shell twin: `czcfg`.
- **Never `chezmoi add` a `modify_`/`create_` target** — it overwrites the script.
- Full command cheat-sheet: `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`. Install-vs-upgrade is
  split: `chezmoi apply`/ansible is **install-only**; upgrades go through
  `just upgrade-*`.

## What's enabled on THIS machine

(Rendered from this host's selections. For live truth: `chezmoi data | jq`.)
- **Coding agents** — Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, Copilot (configs + CLIs). See `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md`, `docs/tools/agent-skills.md`.
- **Python uv tools** — mlflow, marimo, jupyter, etc. (powers the `mlf` CLI). See `docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md`.
- **Extra runtimes** — rust, bun, ruby via mise (+ cargo/gem tools). Node is always present.
- **LLM tools** — Ollama / LiteLLM / local models.
- **JS CLI tools** — standalone npm CLIs (e.g. readability-cli).
- **.NET tools** — .NET SDK (mise) + dotnet global tools.
- **IaC** — Azure CLI, Terraform, OpenTofu.
- **Media** — ffmpeg, ImageMagick, exiftool, libvips.
- **Media control** — nowplaying-cli + switchaudio-osx (macOS) / playerctl (Linux); unlocks full `sysplay`/`sysnow` (built-in `sysvol`/`sysmute` work regardless).
- **Networking** — nmap, mtr, httpie, gping, trippy.
- **Tunnels** — ngrok, cloudflared.
- **Vim mode** — shell modal editing + tmux vim nav (NOT Neovim/editors — those are always vim).

## Custom in-house CLIs (always deployed to `~/.dotfiles/bin`, on PATH)

Each works from any cwd. Run with `--help`, or read `docs/tools/<name>.md`. Full list: `ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_dotfiles/bin/"`.

- **`fleet`** — cross-host ops over your machines: `fleet chezmoi apply`, `fleet hosts`, `fleet tmux`, `fleet info`, `fleet pueue`, `fleet exec`. See `docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-exec.md`, `docs/tools/fleet-hosts.md`.
- **`mlf`** — MLflow umbrella CLI + TUI dashboard (needs Python uv tools). Picker twin: `tv mlflow`.
- **`pqsum`** — pueue queue summary (text / AI / JSON). See `docs/tools/pueue.md`.
- **`x`** — clipboard/file copy-paste-open with cross-platform fallbacks.
- **`view-office`** — open/preview Office docs (.docx/.xlsx/.pptx + legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt) in the terminal; also powers the yazi Office previewer. See `docs/tools/office-viewers.md`.
- **`mi-router`** / **`reyee`** / **`sms`** — read-only router CLIs (Xiaomi MiWiFi / Ruijie Reyee / Huawei HiLink SMS). See `docs/tools/{mi-router,reyee,sms}.md`.
- **`mi-dhcp-bind`** — opt-in **write** companion to `mi-router`: set/remove MiWiFi static DHCP reservations (`bind --self` autodetects this host). See `docs/tools/mi-dhcp-bind.md`.
- **`ping-monitor`** — record ping over time, flag latency spikes. See `docs/tools/ping-monitor.md`.
- **`wake`** — Wake-on-LAN sender: `wake <host>` powers a box on by magic packet (hosts in `~/.config/wake/hosts.toml`). Passive side = `installWakeOnLan` ansible role. See `docs/sysadmin/wake-on-lan.md`.
- **`yth`** — search your YouTube watch history (title/channel/description + captions; Takeout import + optional cookie sync). Picker twin: `tv yth`. See `docs/tools/yth.md`.
- **`dotcfg`** — reconfigure dotfiles prompts (above).
- **`sesh-preview`** — preview helper for the sesh picker.

## Television (`tv`) — fuzzy pickers with custom channels

There are ~40 **custom** channels (system state, fleet, services, infra, agents…)
that you won't discover otherwise. Browse them:

```bash
tv                      # default picker
tv list-channels        # list everything available
tv <channel>            # open one, e.g. tv fleet-hosts | tv mlflow | tv pueue
ls "$(chezmoi source-path)/dot_config/television/cable/"   # the channel definitions
```

Handy ones: `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `pueue`, `ports`, `kill-process`, `services`,
`sessions`, `keybindings`, `aliases`, `git-ops`, `mac-apps`/`linux-apps`. Full
reference: `docs/tools/tv.md`.

## Keybindings & keymaps

- **`bindings`** (shell function) or **`tv keybindings`** — interactive reference.
- **tmux**: `prefix + Space` (or `prefix + e`) opens the action menu;
  `prefix + T` = sesh picker, `prefix + U` = tools. Deep ref: `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md`.
- **shell ZLE widgets**: `Alt+S` sesh sessions, `Alt+T` tools, `Ctrl+R` history (atuin).
- Master reference: `docs/shells/keybindings.md` (also deployed to `~/.config/docs/shells/keybindings.md`).

## Aliases & functions

`alias` to list shell aliases, or `tv aliases`. Catalog: `docs/shells/aliases.md`.
Helpers worth knowing: `chezmoi-cd` (jump to source), `run-for` (time-box a command),
`bindings` (above). App control: `applaunch`/`appquit`/`apprestart`/… (cross-platform).
System audio (cross-platform, built-in): `sysvol`/`sysmute` (+ `sysplay`/`sysnow` with `installMediaControl`); remote mute via `fleet exec --login -- sysmute on`.

## just recipes (run from the source dir)

```bash
cd "$(chezmoi source-path)" && just --list
```

Categories: `chezmoi-*`, `ansible-*`, `upgrade-*` (brew/mise/uv/npm/cargo/…),
`fleet`/`fleet-*`, `gen-prompts` (regenerate prompt scaffolding), `check`/`lint`,
`docker-*`. See `docs/this_repo/cheatsheet.md`.

## Editing rules (don't skip)

Before changing anything under the repo, read `CLAUDE.md` Hard invariants and the
"Cross-file maintenance rules" table — many surfaces have mandatory mirror updates
in the same commit (docs, completions, tool-managers index, this very skill, …).

9	#
10	# Install-only by design — upgrades are `ya pkg upgrade`
11	# (`just upgrade-yazi-plugins`). See docs/tools/office-viewers.md.
12	
13	set -eu
14	export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
15	
16	{{ if eq .chezmoi.os "darwin" -}}
17	if [[ -f /opt/homebrew/bin/brew ]]; then
18	    eval "$(/opt/homebrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
19	elif [[ -f /usr/local/bin/brew ]]; then
20	    eval "$(/usr/local/bin/brew shellenv)"
21	fi
22	{{ else -}}
23	if [[ -d /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew ]]; then
24	    eval "$(/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew shellenv)"
25	elif [[ -d "$HOME/.linuxbrew" ]]; then
26	    eval "$("$HOME/.linuxbrew/bin/brew" shellenv)"
27	fi
28	{{ end -}}
29	
30	info()    { printf '\033[0;34m[INFO]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
31	warn()    { printf '\033[1;33m[WARN]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
32	success() { printf '\033[0;32m[SUCCESS]\033[0m %s\n' "$*"; }
33	
34	# `ya` is yazi's CLI companion (ships with yazi). `ya pkg` replaced the older
35	# `ya pack`. Skip gracefully on fresh boxes where the devtools role hasn't
36	# installed yazi yet (this run-script is 45, ansible roles run at 20).
37	if ! command -v ya >/dev/null 2>&1; then
38	    info "ya (yazi CLI) not found; skipping yazi plugin install (devtools role installs yazi)"
39	    exit 0
40	fi
41	if ! command -v yazi >/dev/null 2>&1; then
42	    info "yazi not found; skipping yazi plugin install"
43	    exit 0
44	fi
45	if [ ! -f "$HOME/.config/yazi/package.toml" ]; then
46	    warn "yazi package.toml not found; skipping (chezmoi apply should deploy it)"
47	    exit 0
48	fi
49	
50	info "Installing yazi plugins from package.toml via \`ya pkg install\`"
51	if ya pkg install >/dev/null 2>&1; then
52	    success "yazi plugins installed"
53	else

55	fi

I have gathered comprehensive details from the README, the plugin's `main.lua` source, and the official Yazi docs. Here is the structured research summary. (This was read-only research — no files were created or modified.)

---

# `wylie102/duckdb.yazi` — Install & Wiring Research

Repo: `github.com/wylie102/duckdb.yazi` · License: MIT. A DuckDB-CLI-powered previewer/preloader for tabular and data files.

## 1. Install command & package.toml

- The README literally shows the **older** syntax: `ya pack -a wylie102/duckdb`.
- The **modern equivalent** (Yazi renamed `ya pack` → `ya pkg`) is:
  ```
  ya pkg add wylie102/duckdb
  ```
  Note the reference is `wylie102/duckdb`, NOT `wylie102/duckdb.yazi` — Yazi's convention strips/appends the `.yazi` suffix automatically. Both commands install the identical package.
- It installs a **single plugin** (`duckdb.yazi`), not a bundle/monorepo subdir. There is no `:subdir` syntax here.
- After adding, `~/.config/yazi/package.toml` gains a locked dependency block of the form:
  ```toml
  [[plugin.deps]]
  use  = "wylie102/duckdb"
  rev  = "<commit-sha>"
  hash = "<integrity-hash>"
  ```
  (The docs' generic example is `use = "owner/my-plugin"`, `rev = "0573024"`, `hash = "..."`.) Keep it updated with `ya pkg upgrade`.

## 2. Required `yazi.toml` config (verbatim from README)

It uses `prepend_previewers` with `run = "duckdb"` — this is the **plugin name** (`duckdb.yazi`), NOT a `piper` piped command. It ALSO requires `prepend_preloaders` (used for cache generation), and there is a **separate `{ ... }` entry per extension** (it does NOT self-declare extensions; the user maps each one).

```toml
[plugin]
prepend_previewers = [
    { name = "*.csv", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.tsv", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.json", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.parquet", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.txt", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.db", run = "duckdb" },
    { name = "*.duckdb", run = "duckdb" }
]

prepend_preloaders = [
    { name = "*.csv", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.tsv", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.json", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.parquet", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.txt", run = "duckdb", multi = false },
    { name = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb", multi = false }
]
```

Notes: `prepend_preloaders` covers only 6 extensions (it excludes `*.db` and `*.duckdb` — database files are not pre-cached). There is **no** `prepend_fetchers` requirement. `multi = false` is set on every preloader entry.

It also needs an **`init.lua`** setup call (required to initialize the plugin):
```lua
require("duckdb"):setup()
-- or with options:
require("duckdb"):setup({
    mode = "standard"/"summarized",   -- Default: "summarized"
    cache_size = 1000,                -- Default: 500
    row_id = true/false/"dynamic",    -- Default: false
    minmax_column_width = int,        -- Default: 21
    column_fit_factor = float,        -- Default: 10.0
})
```

## 3. Targeted extensions (user maps each manually)

Default targets per README and the code's `extension_map`: **csv, tsv, txt, json, parquet, xlsx, db, duckdb**.
- The plugin does **NOT** self-declare/auto-register extensions — each must be listed manually in `prepend_previewers` (and, for the tabular ones, `prepend_preloaders`).
- `.txt` is included only because some tabular files are misnamed `.txt`; the README notes you can omit it if you never need raw-text-as-table.
- `.sqlite` is **NOT** supported (not in the map). `.db` is handled **only if it is an actual DuckDB database** — see #3/#8 caveat below.

## 4. Dependencies (DuckDB CLI + extensions)

- Requires the **`duckdb` CLI binary on PATH**. The README links to DuckDB's install page but does **not state an explicit minimum version number**, and `main.lua` contains **no version check**. Practically, use a recent DuckDB 1.x (the summarize/highlight/`-readonly` behaviors it relies on assume a modern 1.x release).
- Runtime extension usage found in `main.lua`:
  - `install spatial` + `load spatial` — used for **xlsx** reading via `st_read(...)` (chosen over the `excel` extension for more consistent type inference).
  - Core readers `read_csv(...)`, `read_parquet` / `parquet_metadata(...)`, `read_json`, and `SUMMARIZE FROM ...` are built-in to DuckDB.
- **First-run network**: because it runs `INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial`, the **first xlsx preview needs internet** to download the spatial extension from DuckDB's repo (unless already installed/cached in `~/.duckdb`). CSV/TSV/JSON/Parquet/DB previews use built-ins and need **no** network.
- No `sqlite_scanner` / `sqlite` / `excel` extension is installed or loaded anywhere in the code.

## 5. Feather / Arrow (`.feather` / `.arrow`)

**No.** Neither the README nor `main.lua` mentions feather or arrow at all, and they are not in the extension map. DuckDB has no native feather reader, and this plugin does not add one. Not supported.

## 6. Keybindings & features

Bindings are **NOT** shipped in a plugin-owned keymap — the user must add them to their own `keymap.toml` (README-provided block):

```toml
[[manager.prepend_keymap]]
on = "H"
run = "plugin duckdb -1"
desc = "Scroll one column to the left"

[[manager.prepend_keymap]]
on = "L"
run = "plugin duckdb +1"
desc = "Scroll one column to the right"

[[manager.prepend_keymap]]
on = ["g", "o"]
run = "plugin duckdb -open"
desc = "open with duckdb"

[[manager.prepend_keymap]]
on = ["g", "u"]
run = "plugin duckdb -ui"
desc = "open with duckdb ui"
```

Feature notes:
- **Summarized view (SUMMARIZE):** two modes, `standard` and `summarized` (uses DuckDB `SUMMARIZE FROM`). Default mode is set in `init.lua` (`mode = "summarized"` is the plugin default). **Toggle at runtime by pressing `K` while at the top of the file** (this is built into the preview scroll handling, not a separate keymap entry). Vertical row scroll uses `J`/`K`; horizontal **column scroll uses the user-defined `H`/`L`** mapped to `plugin duckdb -1` / `+1`.
- **Row limiting / caching:** on first load it generates Parquet caches for both views (`COPY (...) TO '<cache>' (FORMAT 'parquet')`) to speed scrolling. Standard mode caches `cache_size` rows (default **500**, code: `limit = opts.cache_size or 500`); pagination via `LIMIT %d OFFSET %d`. Other constants: `OFFSET_BASE = 50`, `visible_column_count = 10`, `column_fit_factor = 10`, `minmax_column_width = 21`, internal `cache_version = 3` (baked into `job.skip = 1000000 + cache_version`). README warns that entering a fresh directory triggers cache builds (progress shown bottom-right) during which summarized mode is slower.
- **`g o`** opens the file in the DuckDB CLI; **`g u`** opens the DuckDB UI. Database files (`.db`/`.duckdb`) preview as a table listing (row/column/index counts, PK presence) via `duckdb_tables()` / `duckdb_columns()`, opened read-only (`-readonly`).
- Output highlighting passes through DuckDB's own colors, customizable in `~/.duckdbrc` (e.g. `.highlight_colors column_name magenta bold`, or `.highlight_results off`).

## 7. Conflicts / ordering (e.g. existing `*.xlsx` → `piper -- view-office`)

- `prepend_previewers` **prepends** these rules to the front of Yazi's previewer list. Yazi uses the **first matching** rule, so a prepended `{ name = "*.xlsx", run = "duckdb" }` will **win over** any later/user `*.xlsx` mapping (including a `piper -- view-office` entry) and over Yazi defaults.
- Therefore duckdb.yazi effectively **expects to own xlsx** (and the other listed extensions) once you paste its block. If you want `piper -- view-office` to keep xlsx, **remove the `*.xlsx` line** from duckdb's `prepend_previewers`/`prepend_preloaders`, or use `append_previewers` instead of `prepend_` for one of them so ordering favors the other. Two conflicting `prepend_` entries would resolve by their order within the prepended list (first wins).

## 8. Cross-platform

- No OS-specific install steps — it **just needs the `duckdb` binary on PATH** (macOS and Linux both fine; Windows generally works where DuckDB does).
- README explicitly states highlighting "should now work across any os (where duckdb supports it)," i.e. earlier color issues were resolved; colors depend on your terminal + DuckDB build and are tunable in `~/.duckdbrc`.
- One practical macOS/Linux caveat: the **first xlsx preview downloads the `spatial` extension** (network + write to `~/.duckdb`), so behind a firewall/offline you'd want to pre-run `INSTALL spatial;` once. `.db` support assumes a genuine DuckDB database file — a raw SQLite `.db` will not introspect correctly since the plugin uses `duckdb_tables()` and never loads `sqlite_scanner`.

---

### Key caveats to flag
- README's printed install command is the **legacy** `ya pack -a wylie102/duckdb`; use `ya pkg add wylie102/duckdb` on current Yazi.
- **No pinned minimum DuckDB version** is documented — verify against a recent 1.x yourself.
- **xlsx first-run needs internet** (spatial extension); **.sqlite unsupported**, **.db only if truly DuckDB-format**; **feather/arrow unsupported**.
- Keymap bindings and the `init.lua` setup call are **user-supplied**, not auto-installed by `ya pkg add`.

Relevant source references: README at `raw.githubusercontent.com/wylie102/duckdb.yazi/main/README.md` and `main.lua` at `raw.githubusercontent.com/wylie102/duckdb.yazi/main/main.lua`; Yazi CLI docs at `yazi-rs.github.io/docs/cli/`.
</output>

453	  return "$any_fail"
454	}

456	# ============================================================================
457	# Category: cargo — `cargo install-update -a` (bootstraps cargo-update if needed)
458	# ============================================================================
459	cat_cargo() {
460	  if ! command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
461	    # mise-managed rust shim?
462	    if [[ -x "$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/cargo" ]]; then
463	      export PATH="$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims:$PATH"
464	    elif [[ -x "$HOME/.cargo/bin/cargo" ]]; then
465	      export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH"
466	    else
467	      warn "cargo not found — skipping"
468	      return $SKIP_RC
469	    fi
470	  fi
471	
472	  local any_fail=0
473	  local have_update_tool=0
474	  if command -v cargo-install-update >/dev/null 2>&1; then
475	    have_update_tool=1
476	  else
477	    info "Bootstrapping cargo-update (needed for 'cargo install-update -a')"
478	    if _run cargo install cargo-update; then
479	      # In dry-run, the binary won't materialise — assume success.
480	      if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]] \
481	        || command -v cargo-install-update >/dev/null 2>&1; then
482	        have_update_tool=1
483	      fi
484	    else
485	      any_fail=1
486	    fi
487	  fi
488	
489	  if [[ "$have_update_tool" -eq 1 ]]; then
490	    info "Upgrading all cargo-installed binaries"
491	    _run cargo install-update -a || any_fail=1
492	  else
493	    warn "cargo-update not available; skipping bulk upgrade"
494	    any_fail=1
495	  fi
496	  return "$any_fail"
497	}

499	# ============================================================================
500	# Category: go — `go install <pkg>@latest` for each tool in
501	# dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml
502	# ============================================================================
503	cat_go() {
504	  # Resolve go via mise shim first, then system PATH.
505	  local go_cmd=""
506	  if [[ -x "$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/go" ]]; then
507	    go_cmd="$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/go"
508	  elif command -v go >/dev/null 2>&1; then
509	    go_cmd="go"
510	  else
511	    warn "go not found (Go not installed via mise?) — skipping"
512	    return $SKIP_RC
513	  fi
514	
515	  # Parse the tools list from defaults YAML — lines `  - name: <pkg>@<ver>`.
516	  # Same hand-rolled awk parser as cat_dotnet.
517	  local defaults_file="$_REPO_ROOT/dot_ansible/roles/go_tools/defaults/main.yml"
518	  local tools=()
519	  if [[ -f "$defaults_file" ]]; then
520	    while IFS= read -r line; do
521	      tools+=("$line")
522	    done < <(awk '
523	            /^go_tools:/ { in_list=1; next }
524	            in_list && /^[^ ]/ { in_list=0 }
525	            in_list && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:/ {
526	                sub(/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:[[:space:]]*/, "")
527	                gsub(/["'"'"']/, "")
528	                print
529	            }
530	        ' "$defaults_file")
531	  fi
532	
533	  if [[ ${#tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
534	    warn "no go tools to upgrade — skipping"
535	    return $SKIP_RC
536	  fi
537	
538	  # Install into ~/.local/bin (the blessed dir), not ~/go/bin or the mise
539	  # toolchain dir. Upgrade = re-install at @latest regardless of the version
540	  # pinned in defaults (install-vs-upgrade split — defaults pin for fresh
541	  # installs, this moves them forward). See docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md.
542	  # GOPATH pinned to ~/.local/share/go (XDG data) so the build-time module cache
543	  # doesn't repopulate ~/go — mirrors dot_config/shell/02_legacy_tools.sh and the
544	  # go_tools ansible role.
545	  export GOBIN="$HOME/.local/bin"
546	  export GOPATH="$HOME/.local/share/go"
547	
548	  local any_fail=0
549	  for t in "${tools[@]}"; do
550	    # Strip any @version pin (module paths never contain '@') and go to @latest.
551	    local pkg="${t%@*}"
552	    info "Upgrading go tool: $pkg@latest"
553	    _run "$go_cmd" install "$pkg@latest" || any_fail=1
554	  done
555	  return "$any_fail"
556	}

559	# Category: dotnet — upgrade each tool in dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml
560	# ============================================================================
561	cat_dotnet() {
562	  # Resolve dotnet via mise shim first, then system PATH.
563	  local dotnet_cmd=""
564	  if [[ -x "$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/dotnet" ]]; then
565	    dotnet_cmd="$HOME/.local/share/mise/shims/dotnet"
566	  elif command -v dotnet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
567	    dotnet_cmd="dotnet"
568	  else
569	    warn "dotnet not found — skipping"
570	    return $SKIP_RC
571	  fi
572	
573	  # Parse the tools list from defaults YAML. Small hand-rolled parser: we
574	  # only need lines of the form `  - name: <pkg>`. If parsing produces no
575	  # results, fall back to `dotnet tool list --global`.
576	  local defaults_file="$_REPO_ROOT/dot_ansible/roles/dotnet_tools/defaults/main.yml"
577	  local tools=()
578	  if [[ -f "$defaults_file" ]]; then
579	    while IFS= read -r line; do
580	      tools+=("$line")
581	    done < <(awk '
582	            /^dotnet_tools:/ { in_list=1; next }
583	            in_list && /^[^ ]/ { in_list=0 }
584	            in_list && /^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:/ {
585	                sub(/^[[:space:]]*-[[:space:]]*name:[[:space:]]*/, "")
586	                gsub(/["'"'"']/, "")
587	                print
588	            }
589	        ' "$defaults_file")
590	  fi
591	
592	  if [[ ${#tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
593	    info "Falling back to 'dotnet tool list --global'"
594	    if ! mapfile -t tools < <("$dotnet_cmd" tool list --global 2>/dev/null \
595	      | awk 'NR>2 && NF>0 {print $1}'); then
596	      warn "could not enumerate dotnet tools"
597	      return $SKIP_RC
598	    fi
599	  fi
600	
601	  if [[ ${#tools[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
602	    warn "no dotnet tools to upgrade — skipping"
603	    return $SKIP_RC
604	  fi
605	
606	  # dotnet tools land under ~/.dotnet/tools.
607	  export PATH="$HOME/.dotnet/tools:$PATH"
608	
609	  local any_fail=0
610	  for t in "${tools[@]}"; do
611	    info "Upgrading dotnet tool: $t"
612	    _run "$dotnet_cmd" tool update --global "$t" || any_fail=1
613	  done
614	  return "$any_fail"
615	}

640	# Category: flatpak — `flatpak update` for user-scope Flathub apps
641	# ============================================================================
642	# We deliberately stick to user-scope (`--user`): no sudo required, and our
643	# ansible role installs everything via `method: user`. System-scope flatpaks
644	# need `sudo flatpak update --system`, which the user can run manually if
645	# they have any (rare in this repo's flow).
646	cat_flatpak() {
647	  if ! command -v flatpak >/dev/null 2>&1; then
648	    warn "flatpak not installed — skipping"
649	    return $SKIP_RC
650	  fi
651	
652	  # Skip silently when there's nothing user-scoped to update — avoids logging
653	  # a "Nothing to do." into upgrade summaries on machines that have never set
654	  # discordChannel=flatpak.
655	  local n_user_apps
656	  n_user_apps="$(flatpak list --app --user 2>/dev/null | wc -l)"
657	  if [[ "$n_user_apps" -eq 0 ]]; then
658	    info "No user-scope Flatpak apps installed — skipping"
659	    return $SKIP_RC
660	  fi
661	
662	  local any_fail=0
663	  info "Upgrading user-scope Flatpak apps ($n_user_apps installed)"
664	  _run flatpak update --user --noninteractive --assumeyes || any_fail=1
665	  return "$any_fail"
666	}

668	# ============================================================================
669	# Category: warp — Linux apt-only upgrade for Warp Terminal
670	# ============================================================================
671	# macOS Warp is handled by `cat_brew` (cask "warp" + --greedy). On Linux,
672	# Warp's only supported channel is its own apt repo, but the in-app updater
673	# pastes `... && warp_finish_update <token>` into the prompt — that token is
674	# only valid inside a live Warp session and `warp_finish_update` is a
675	# Warp-injected shell function (not on PATH otherwise). So this category
676	# does the apt half only and leaves the user to restart Warp themselves.
677	#
678	# See docs/tools/warp.md for the full mechanism (token IPC handshake, etc.).
679	cat_warp() {
680	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Linux" ]]; then
681	    info "Not Linux — Warp is upgraded via brew cask, skipping"
682	    return $SKIP_RC
683	  fi
684	  if ! command -v warp-terminal >/dev/null 2>&1; then
685	    warn "warp-terminal not installed — skipping"
686	    return $SKIP_RC
687	  fi
688	
689	  # warp-terminal is gated behind sudo apt. Reuse the shared sudo session so
690	  # the user isn't re-prompted across upgrade categories.
691	  if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 0 ]] && declare -F sudo_session_init >/dev/null 2>&1; then
692	    if ! sudo_session_init "upgrade-warp"; then
693	      warn "Sudo session could not be established — skipping"
694	      return $SKIP_RC
695	    fi
696	    case "$(sudo_session_skip_reason)" in
697	      non-interactive | "")
698	        warn "Non-interactive mode without passwordless sudo — skipping warp"
699	        return $SKIP_RC
700	        ;;
701	    esac
702	  fi
703	
704	  local any_fail=0
705	  info "Refreshing Warp apt repo + installing only the warp-terminal candidate"
706	  # `apt update` covers all repos (cheap; usually run once per session anyway).
707	  _run sudo apt-get update || any_fail=1
708	  # `--only-upgrade` ensures we never accidentally re-install if the package
709	  # was uninstalled between commands; `-y` is safe because we're pinned to
710	  # one package name.
711	  _run sudo apt-get install --only-upgrade -y warp-terminal || any_fail=1
712	
713	  if [[ "$any_fail" -eq 0 ]]; then
714	    info "Warp on-disk binary updated. Quit + relaunch Warp to load the new version."
715	    info "(The in-app 'warp_finish_update <token>' graceful-restart only works from inside Warp.)"
716	  fi
717	  return "$any_fail"
718	}

722	# ============================================================================
723	# macOS path is covered by `brew upgrade atuin` in cat_brew. This category
724	# only does work on Linux, where atuin was installed via the official
725	# https://setup.atuin.sh installer (see dot_ansible/roles/atuin/).

729	    return $SKIP_RC
730	  fi
731	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" != "Linux" ]]; then
732	    info "Not Linux — atuin upgraded via brew (cat_brew), skipping"
733	    return $SKIP_RC
734	  fi
735	
736	  local any_fail=0
737	  # `atuin update` (subcommand) is the upstream-recommended self-upgrade for
738	  # installer-based installs. Falls back to re-running the installer.
739	  info "Upgrading atuin (Linux, official installer)"
740	  if ! _run atuin update; then
741	    warn "atuin update failed; falling back to installer re-run"
742	    if ! _run_sh 'curl --proto "=https" --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://setup.atuin.sh | sh -s -- --non-interactive'; then
743	      any_fail=1
744	      error "atuin installer re-run failed"
745	    fi
746	  fi
747	  return "$any_fail"
748	}

751	# Category: yazi-plugins — `ya pkg upgrade` for Yazi plugins (piper.yazi, …)
752	# ============================================================================
753	# `chezmoi apply` is install-only: it materializes plugins from the pinned
754	# lockfile (dot_config/yazi/package.toml) via `ya pkg install`. This category
755	# bumps them to the latest upstream revs. Remember to copy the regenerated
756	# ~/.config/yazi/package.toml back into the chezmoi source afterward, else the
757	# next apply pins the old rev again. See docs/tools/office-viewers.md.
758	cat_yazi_plugins() {

760	    warn "ya (yazi CLI) not installed — skipping"

764	    warn "no ~/.config/yazi/package.toml — no yazi plugins to upgrade, skipping"
765	    return $SKIP_RC
766	  fi
767	  info "Upgrading Yazi plugins (ya pkg upgrade)"
768	  if ! _run ya pkg upgrade; then
769	    error "ya pkg upgrade failed"
770	    return 1
771	  fi
772	  warn "Remember: copy ~/.config/yazi/package.toml into the chezmoi source to persist new revs"
773	  return 0

776	# ============================================================================
777	# Category: agents — re-run install.sh for curl-installed CLI tools
778	# ============================================================================
779	# Only re-runs when the binary is already present. The installers are (by
780	# design) idempotent self-upgrades.
781	cat_agents() {
782	  local any_fail=0
783	  local ran_any=0
784	
785	  # Strategy: prefer the binary's built-in self-update subcommand (fast no-op
786	  # when already current; doesn't re-download the full binary). Fallback to
787	  # the official curl installer if the subcommand fails, hangs, or doesn't
788	  # exist. Inspection of upstream installers (2026-04) confirmed none of them
789	  # delegate to the self-update subcommand internally:
790	  #   - claude.sh   : always re-downloads, no version check
791	  #   - opencode.sh : has a same-version fast-path, but no `opencode upgrade`
792	  #   - cursor.sh   : always re-downloads, no version check
793	  #
794	  # We wrap the self-update call with a timeout (some `claude update` runs
795	  # have been observed hanging indefinitely on network checks) so a stuck
796	  # subcommand cannot block the whole upgrade flow.
797	  local _timeout_bin=""
798	  if command -v timeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
799	    _timeout_bin="timeout"
800	  elif command -v gtimeout >/dev/null 2>&1; then
801	    _timeout_bin="gtimeout"
802	  fi
803	  _try_self_update_then_curl() {
804	    local label="$1" self_cmd="$2" curl_url="$3"
805	    info "Upgrading $label (trying self-update first)"
806	    local wrapped="$self_cmd"
807	    if [[ -n "$_timeout_bin" ]]; then
808	      wrapped="$_timeout_bin 90 $self_cmd"
809	    fi
810	    if _run_sh "$wrapped"; then
811	      return 0
812	    fi
813	    warn "$label self-update failed/timed out — falling back to official installer"
814	    local fallback="curl -fsSL $curl_url | bash"
815	    if [[ -n "$_timeout_bin" ]]; then
816	      fallback="$_timeout_bin 300 bash -c 'curl -fsSL $curl_url | bash'"
817	    fi
818	    _run_sh "$fallback"
819	  }
820	
821	  # Claude Code — `claude update` (alias: `claude upgrade`)
822	  if command -v claude >/dev/null 2>&1 \
823	    || [[ -x "$HOME/.claude/local/bin/claude" ]]; then
824	    _try_self_update_then_curl "Claude Code" \
825	      "claude update" \
826	      "https://claude.ai/install.sh" || any_fail=1
827	    ran_any=1
828	  fi
829	
830	  # OpenCode — `opencode upgrade`
831	  if command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
832	    _try_self_update_then_curl "OpenCode" \
833	      "opencode upgrade" \
834	      "https://opencode.ai/install" || any_fail=1
835	    ran_any=1
836	  fi
837	
838	  # Cursor CLI — `cursor-agent update`
839	  if command -v cursor-agent >/dev/null 2>&1 \
840	    || command -v cursor-cli >/dev/null 2>&1 \
841	    || [[ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/cursor-agent" ]]; then
842	    _try_self_update_then_curl "Cursor CLI" \
843	      "cursor-agent update" \
844	      "https://cursor.com/install" || any_fail=1
845	    ran_any=1
846	  fi
847	
848	  # Ollama — Linux official installer (macOS is Homebrew-managed elsewhere).
849	  # No self-update subcommand exists.
850	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Linux" ]] && command -v ollama >/dev/null 2>&1; then
851	    info "Upgrading Ollama (Linux installer)"
852	    _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh" || any_fail=1
853	    ran_any=1
854	  fi
855	
856	  # llmfit — official local installer (Linux; macOS uses Homebrew)
857	  if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Linux" ]] && command -v llmfit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
858	    info "Upgrading llmfit (Linux local installer)"
859	    _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://llmfit.axjns.dev/install.sh | sh -s -- --local" || any_fail=1
860	    ran_any=1
861	  fi
862	
863	  # RTK — official installer (no self-update subcommand)
864	  if command -v rtk >/dev/null 2>&1; then
865	    info "Upgrading RTK"
866	    _run_sh "curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rtk-ai/rtk/refs/heads/master/install.sh | sh" || any_fail=1
867	    ran_any=1
868	  fi
869	
870	  # SpecStory — brew tap when available (macOS), else GitHub release script.
871	  # The installer script is idempotent and pulls latest by default, so re-running
872	  # it is the upgrade path on Linux (and on macOS when not brew-managed).
873	  if command -v specstory >/dev/null 2>&1 \
874	    || [[ -x "$HOME/.local/bin/specstory" ]]; then
875	    local specstory_handled=0
876	    if [[ "$(uname -s)" == "Darwin" ]] && setup_brew_path \
877	      && brew list --formula specstoryai/tap/specstory >/dev/null 2>&1; then
878	      info "Upgrading SpecStory via Homebrew tap"
879	      _run brew upgrade specstoryai/tap/specstory || any_fail=1
880	      specstory_handled=1
881	    fi
882	    if [[ "$specstory_handled" -eq 0 ]]; then
883	      if [[ -x "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/install_specstory.sh" ]]; then
884	        info "Upgrading SpecStory via install_specstory.sh (latest GitHub release)"
885	        _run "$_REPO_ROOT/scripts/install_specstory.sh" || any_fail=1
886	      else
887	        warn "specstory present but install_specstory.sh not found — skipping"
888	      fi
889	    fi
890	    ran_any=1
891	  fi
892	
893	  if [[ "$ran_any" -eq 0 ]]; then
894	    warn "no known curl-installed agents detected — skipping"
895	    return $SKIP_RC
896	  fi
897	
898	  return "$any_fail"
899	}

901	# ============================================================================
902	# Category: plugins — editor/tmux/pre-commit/tldr/gh plugin upgrades
903	# ============================================================================
904	cat_plugins() {
905	  local any_fail=0
906	  local ran_any=0
907	  local claude_hud_helper="$_REPO_ROOT/dot_ansible/roles/coding_agents/files/claude_hud_sync.py"
908	  local claude_hud_installed=0

910	  # LazyVim (Neovim plugins)

912	    info "Syncing LazyVim plugins (nvim --headless +Lazy! sync +qa)"

915	    ran_any=1

920	    info "Updating tmux plugins via TPM"
921	    _run "$HOME/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/update_plugins" all || any_fail=1
922	    ran_any=1

925	  # claude-hud plugin cache / installed_plugins.json
926	  if [[ -d "$HOME/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-hud" ]]; then
927	    claude_hud_installed=1
928	  elif [[ -f "$HOME/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json" ]] \
929	    && grep -q '"claude-hud@claude-hud"' "$HOME/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json"; then
930	    claude_hud_installed=1
931	  fi
932	  if [[ "$claude_hud_installed" -eq 1 ]] \
933	    && command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 \
934	    && [[ -f "$claude_hud_helper" ]]; then
935	    info "Refreshing claude-hud plugin"
936	    _run python3 "$claude_hud_helper" --only-if-installed || any_fail=1
937	    ran_any=1
938	  fi
939	
940	  # pre-commit autoupdate — only when we're in the dotfiles repo itself
941	  if command -v pre-commit >/dev/null 2>&1 \
942	    && [[ -f "$_REPO_ROOT/.pre-commit-config.yaml" ]]; then
943	    info "Running pre-commit autoupdate on the dotfiles repo"
944	    (cd "$_REPO_ROOT" && _run pre-commit autoupdate) || any_fail=1
945	    ran_any=1
946	  fi
947	
948	  # tldr cache
949	  if command -v tldr >/dev/null 2>&1; then
950	    info "Updating tldr cache"
951	    _run tldr --update || any_fail=1
952	    ran_any=1
953	  fi
954	
955	  # gh extensions
956	  if command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
957	    info "Upgrading gh extensions"
958	    _run gh extension upgrade --all || any_fail=1
959	    ran_any=1
960	  fi
961	
962	  if [[ "$ran_any" -eq 0 ]]; then
963	    warn "no plugin managers detected — skipping"
964	    return $SKIP_RC
965	  fi
966	  return "$any_fail"
967	}

969	# ============================================================================
970	# Main: dispatch selected categories in defined order
971	# ============================================================================
972	hr
973	if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
974	  info "upgrade_tools.sh — categories: ${SELECTED[*]} (dry-run)"
975	else
976	  info "upgrade_tools.sh — categories: ${SELECTED[*]}"
977	fi
978	if [[ "$DRY_RUN" -eq 1 ]]; then
979	  warn "DRY-RUN MODE — commands are printed, not executed"
980	fi
981	
982	# Run in the canonical ALL_CATEGORIES order (regardless of CLI arg order).
983	for cat in "${ALL_CATEGORIES[@]}"; do
984	  for sel in "${SELECTED[@]}"; do
985	    if [[ "$cat" == "$sel" ]]; then
986	      case "$cat" in

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# view-office — open or preview Microsoft Office / OpenDocument files in the
3	# terminal. Dispatches by extension to the right tool:
4	#   .docx → doxx        .xlsx → visidata (vd)   .pptx → markitdown | glow
5	#   legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt/.odt/.ods/.odp/.rtf → LibreOffice headless converts to
6	#   the modern OOXML twin, then re-dispatches to the handler above.
7	#
8	# Two modes:
9	#   view-office FILE              interactive TUI / pager (default)
10	#   view-office --preview FILE    non-interactive ANSI/markdown to stdout
11	#
12	# Deliberately plain bash, NOT the `uv run --script` self-boot pattern used by
13	# executable_pqsum / yth / mlf: this sits on yazi's preview hot-path (invoked on
14	# every file hover via the piper.yazi previewer), where uv/Python startup
15	# (~100-200ms) would make previews feel laggy. Pure dispatch/exec is ~5ms.
16	#
17	# The yazi previewer contract (dot_config/yazi/yazi.toml) is:
18	#   run = 'piper -- view-office --preview --width "$w" "$1"'
19	# Keep --preview/--width in sync with that. See docs/tools/office-viewers.md.
20	set -euo pipefail
21	
22	PREVIEW=0
23	WIDTH="${COLUMNS:-100}"
24	
25	usage() {
26	    printf '%s\n' \
27	        "Usage: view-office [--preview] [--width N] FILE" \
28	        "" \
29	        "Open or preview an Office / OpenDocument file in the terminal." \
30	        "" \
31	        "Options:" \
32	        "  -p, --preview    Render to stdout (ANSI/markdown) instead of a TUI." \
33	        "  -w, --width N    Wrap width for --preview (default: \$COLUMNS or 100)." \
34	        "  -h, --help       Show this help." \
35	        "" \
36	        "Formats:" \
37	        "  .docx  doxx (interactive) / doxx --export ansi (preview)" \
38	        "  .xlsx  visidata vd (interactive) / markitdown | glow (preview)" \
39	        "  .pptx  markitdown | glow pager (interactive) / markitdown | glow (preview)" \
40	        "  .doc .xls .ppt .odt .ods .odp .rtf  LibreOffice → OOXML twin, then above"
41	}
42	
43	err() { printf 'view-office: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
44	
45	have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }
46	
47	# need TOOL "install hint" — fail with an actionable message if TOOL is absent.
48	need() {
49	    have "$1" && return 0
50	    err "$1 not found — $2"
51	    exit 2
52	}
53	
54	# Resolve the LibreOffice headless binary: `soffice` / `libreoffice` on PATH,
55	# else the macOS .app bundle (the cask does not put soffice on PATH).
56	soffice_bin() {
57	    local b
58	    for b in soffice libreoffice; do
59	        if have "$b"; then printf '%s\n' "$b"; return 0; fi
60	    done
61	    if [[ -x /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice ]]; then
62	        printf '%s\n' /Applications/LibreOffice.app/Contents/MacOS/soffice
63	        return 0
64	    fi
65	    return 1
66	}
67	
68	# Render markdown from stdin: pretty ANSI via glow if present, else raw passthrough.
69	render_md() {
70	    if have glow; then
71	        glow -w "$WIDTH" -
72	    else
73	        cat
74	    fi
75	}
76	
77	render_docx() {
78	    local f="$1"
79	    need doxx "install via the devtools ansible role (brew bgreenwell/tap/doxx)"
80	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
81	        doxx --export ansi -w "$WIDTH" "$f"
82	    else
83	        doxx "$f"
84	    fi
85	}
86	
87	render_xlsx() {
88	    local f="$1"
89	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
90	        need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
91	        markitdown "$f" | render_md
92	    else
93	        need vd "install visidata via python_uv_tools (uv tool install visidata)"
94	        vd "$f"
95	    fi
96	}
97	
98	render_pptx() {
99	    local f="$1"
100	    need markitdown "install via python_uv_tools (uv tool install markitdown)"
101	    if ((PREVIEW)); then
102	        markitdown "$f" | render_md
103	    elif have glow; then
104	        markitdown "$f" | glow -p -
105	    else
106	        markitdown "$f" | "${PAGER:-less}"
107	    fi
108	}
109	
110	# Legacy binary / OpenDocument formats: convert to the modern OOXML twin with
111	# LibreOffice headless (isolated -env profile so a running GUI instance doesn't
112	# lock us out), then re-dispatch. NOTE: we run the viewer as a child (no exec)
113	# so the EXIT trap still fires and cleans the tmpdir after an interactive TUI.
114	render_legacy() {
115	    local f="$1" target="$2" so tmp stem twin
116	    so="$(soffice_bin)" || {
117	        err "LibreOffice (soffice) not found — install via the devtools role (brew --cask libreoffice / apt libreoffice)"
118	        exit 2
119	    }
120	    tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
121	    trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT
122	    if ! "$so" --headless -env:UserInstallation="file://$tmp/profile" \
123	            --convert-to "$target" --outdir "$tmp" "$f" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
124	        err "LibreOffice failed to convert $f → $target"
125	        exit 1
126	    fi
127	    stem="$(basename -- "$f")"; stem="${stem%.*}"
128	    twin="$tmp/$stem.$target"
129	    [[ -f "$twin" ]] || { err "converted file not found: $twin"; exit 1; }
130	    render "$twin"
131	}
132	
133	render() {
134	    local f="$1" ext
135	    ext="${f##*.}"
136	    ext="$(printf '%s' "$ext" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"  # bash 3.2-safe lowercasing
137	    case "$ext" in
138	        docx)        render_docx "$f" ;;
139	        xlsx)        render_xlsx "$f" ;;
140	        pptx)        render_pptx "$f" ;;
141	        doc|odt|rtf) render_legacy "$f" docx ;;
142	        xls|ods)     render_legacy "$f" xlsx ;;
143	        ppt|odp)     render_legacy "$f" pptx ;;
144	        *)
145	            err "unsupported file type: .$ext"
146	            err "supported: docx xlsx pptx doc xls ppt odt ods odp rtf"
147	            exit 2
148	            ;;
149	    esac
150	}
151	
152	main() {
153	    local file=""
154	    while (($#)); do
155	        case "$1" in
156	            -p|--preview) PREVIEW=1; shift ;;
157	            -w|--width)
158	                [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { err "--width requires a value"; exit 2; }
159	                WIDTH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
160	            --width=*) WIDTH="${1#*=}"; shift ;;
161	            -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
162	            --) shift; while (($#)); do file="$1"; shift; done; break ;;
163	            -*) err "unknown option: $1"; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
164	            *)
165	                if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then file="$1"; else err "too many files: $1"; exit 2; fi
166	                shift ;;
167	        esac
168	    done
169	
170	    if [[ -z "$file" ]]; then
171	        err "expected a FILE"
172	        usage >&2
173	        exit 2
174	    fi
175	    if [[ ! -r "$file" ]]; then
176	        err "file not readable: $file"
177	        exit 1
178	    fi
179	    render "$file"
180	}
181	
182	main "$@"
183
```

When adding a NEW agent, update: SSOT (one new `AICAP_<AGENT>_MODEL` line), `04_ai_capture.sh:_aiagent_invoke` case, **all four** Python `AGENT_CONFIG` dicts. **Four consumers = pain threshold reached** — the extraction TODO (`scripts/aisum/__init__.py`) is now blocking ergonomics; next AI-tooling change should land that refactor before adding more callsites. | — |
30	| chezmoi-apply reload hint: `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_after_99_signal_reload.sh.tmpl` (touches sentinel) ↔ `dot_config/shell/99_chezmoi_reload.sh` (reads sentinel + zsh/bash hook registration + `cas`/`cau` wrappers) | Row in [docs/shells/aliases.md](docs/shells/aliases.md) "Dotfiles management" section for `cas`/`cau` | The sentinel path `~/.cache/chezmoi/last-apply` is hard-coded in **two** places — the run-script that touches it and the shared backend that reads it. Keep both in sync when relocating (e.g. switching to `$XDG_STATE_HOME`). Hook registration is in the shared backend (NOT `dot_config/{zsh,bash}/99_*`) because bash's `$BASH_CONFIG_DIR` loads before `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/shell` (oh-my-bash `plugins=()` prereq, see `dot_bashrc.tmpl:94` vs `:114`), so a per-shell hook file in `dot_config/bash/` would run before the backend function exists. Opt out: `export CHEZMOI_RELOAD_HINT=0`. |
31	| `app-*` helpers — `dot_config/shell/54_macos_apps.sh.tmpl` (macOS) ↔ `dot_config/shell/56_linux_apps.sh.tmpl` (Linux) ↔ `dot_config/television/cable/mac-apps.toml.tmpl` ↔ `dot_config/television/cable/linux-apps.toml.tmpl` | Both shell helpers MUST expose the SAME public verb names (`appquit` / `applaunch` / `appactivate` / `apprestart` / `apprunning` / `applist` / `appresponsive`) so users get cross-platform muscle memory. Backends diverge by necessity (Apple Events vs `gtk-launch` + `pkill -TERM` + optional GNOME `window-calls` ext). Adding a new verb to one side: decide whether it can also be implemented on the other; if not, document the gap in `backlog/linux-desktop-app-control.md` "Open follow-ups". Both `tv` channel files MUST share Alt-key bindings where the verb exists on both sides — **Alt+H is mac-only by design** (Linux can't hide windows without compositor IPC; the Alt+H slot stays free on `tv linux-apps`). Per-app overrides for Linux AppImage/Snap/Flatpak runtime paths live in `~/.config/shell/linux-apps.conf` (not auto-stubbed, matches `.shellrc.secrets` rule) — never auto-generate this file from the helper. | [docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md](docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md) "Controlling installed apps from the shell" section; [pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md](pitfalls/linux-app-control-appimage-runtime-path.md), [pitfalls/linux-app-control-gapplication-zero-coverage.md](pitfalls/linux-app-control-gapplication-zero-coverage.md). Empirical baseline: `gapplication list-apps` returns only ~13 GNOME-core apps on Ubuntu 24.04 Wayland — third-party Electron/AppImage/Snap/Flatpak coverage is **zero**, so don't reach for `gapplication action … quit` as the primary mechanism. |
32	| Docker `registry-mirrors` list in `dot_config/docker/modify_daemon.json.tmpl` (canonical) | Full list + per-mirror notes in [docs/tools/containers.md](docs/tools/containers.md) + `.zh-TW` (Strategy A JSON block + bullets), and the coverage-matrix Docker row + § Security and trust model in [docs/tools/mirrors.md](docs/tools/mirrors.md) + `.zh-TW` | When dropping/adding a mirror, state the **security** reason, not just speed: a pull-through mirror resolves `tag→digest` and Docker Content Trust is off by default, so a dead/third-party mirror domain risks lapsing → re-registration into a malicious pull-through cache. Curated high-reputation set only; `azk8s`/`dockerproxy` removed 2026-07 for this. |
33	
34	**Repo-root files that stay OUT of MkDocs nav** (`README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md`, `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/`, `NOTES.md`): referenced via absolute GitHub URLs from [`docs/for-maintainers.md`](docs/for-maintainers.md), never copied via `pymdownx.snippets`.
35	
36	**Three-tier file placement** for new shell helpers:
37	
38	| Tier | Dir | When |
39	|---|---|---|
40	| Shared | `dot_config/shell/` | POSIX subset, both shells source. `$ZSH_VERSION`/`$BASH_VERSION` source-time dispatch is OK; ZLE widgets / `compdef` / `bindkey` / `setopt` / `read -q` / `${m:t}` / glob qualifiers are NOT (bash would error on source). |
41	| Zsh-only | `dot_config/zsh/` | ZLE widgets, `compdef`, `bindkey`, `setopt`, zsh-vi-mode hooks. |
42	| Bash-only | `dot_config/bash/` | `bind -x` / `ble-bind`, OMB plugin arrays, bash-specific `shopt`s. |
43	
44	When porting a zsh-only helper to bash via ble.sh, extract the shell-agnostic backend into `dot_config/shell/` and keep each shell's widget binding in its own dir.

46	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
47	
48	Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):
49	
50	1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
51	2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
52	3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
53	4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
54	5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
55	6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers
56	
57	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.
58	
59	### Long-term backlog + past pitfalls → use the `project-knowledge-harness` skill
60	
61	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply` via `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`; see [docs/tools/agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template, disambiguation table, and upgrade path.
62	
63	**Fallback rules** so this section still binds when the skill cannot be loaded:
64	
65	- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (priority/effort tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (research/design notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
66	- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
67	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
68	- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it (a) recurs across machines, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.

70	## Chezmoi templating conventions
71	
72	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
73	
74	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
75	
76	| Predicate | Use |
77	|---|---|
78	| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
79	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
80	| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
81	| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
82	| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |
83	
84	Decision table, before/after examples, `macos_intel` migration: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
85	
86	## Hard repo invariants
87	
88	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
89	
90	Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
91	
92	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
93	
94	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
95	
96	**Hard rules**:
97	
98	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
99	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
100	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
101	
102	ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
103	
104	### Three-tier user-local override layer
105	
106	User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
107	
108	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`:
109	
110	```
111	managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc
112	```
113	
114	Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
115	
116	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
117	
118	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
119	
120	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templated files + 2 first-seed files (`marimo.toml`, btop's `btop.conf`): [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
121	
122	**Hard rules**:
123	
124	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
125	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, `dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`, `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
126	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
127	- The `minimal` bundle in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without explicit user request.
128	- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.
129	
130	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
131	
132	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
133	
134	**Hard rules**:
135	
136	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
137	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
138	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a single tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it legitimately needs a newer version (e.g. `python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5` for `--with-executables-from`). MUST detect install style (brew vs curl/standalone) and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors if not a brew formula). Dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`. See [docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
139	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`. Without it the install guard short-circuits on hosts where the primary binary already exists, and entry-point shims are never written (silent missing `jupyter` / `jupyter-notebook` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit: `yq '.python_uv_tools[] | select(.with_executables_from) | select(.extra_binaries == null) | .name' …` MUST print nothing. See [pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
140	- New upgrade category: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md → Adding a new category](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). For a tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise: do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.
141	
142	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
143	
144	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
145	
146	**Hard rules**:
147	
148	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
149	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
150	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
151	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
152	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
153	
154	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**:
155	
156	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
157	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag.
158	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
159	4. Privileged commands via `sudo_run …` or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible.
160	
161	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. **Never** read `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` directly — always go through `sudo_session_init`. Full API + state + cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
162	
163	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
164	
165	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
166	
167	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — but it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let template win.
168	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
169	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS the user's editor working tree). Local hosts log warn and run against working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
170	- **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
171	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
172	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
173	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
174	  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
175	  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
176	  - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
177	  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
178	
179	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
180	
181	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (tomlkit overlay — managed tables enforced, herdr's runtime writeback preserved), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
182	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
183	
184	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
185	
186	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
187	
188	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
189	
190	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
191	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
192	
193	**Hard rules**:
194	
195	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
196	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
197	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
198	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
199	
200	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
201	
202	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
203	
204	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
205	
206	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
207	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
208	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
209	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
210	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
211	
212	Full tmux config breakdown / theme switching / keybindings / troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
213	
214	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
215	
216	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner apps by default. `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. First Zellij launch (no existing config): select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.
217
```
